summary.clip_miss_explanation: Three counties show S1100 features in the bounding-box query that drop to 0 after polygon intersection. This is not necessarily wrong — roads along a county line drawn in one dataset may fall marginally outside the polygon of another — but it has not been independently verified by visual inspection or cross-reference to a second boundary source. The results for these three counties are labeled no_primary_roads, which may be correct or may understate their primary-road network.

3_nfhl_retrieval.verdict: Retrieval is complete by ID-batch strategy; SFHA_TF filter correct; coastal VE zones are included and not excluded
3_nfhl_retrieval.coastal_treatment: VE (velocity/wave coastal) zones are INCLUDED in the flood footprint. The pipeline WHERE clause is SFHA_TF='T', which captures all Special Flood Hazard Areas regardless of whether they are riverine (AE/A) or coastal (VE). The pipeline does not distinguish or exclude coastal flooding.
3_nfhl_retrieval.inland_flood_scope_issue: This pipeline is labeled 'inland flood'. VE zones represent storm-surge and wave-action coastal flooding, not riverine/pluvial inland flooding. Including VE zones overstates inland flood exposure for the 9 coastal counties. The magnitude of overstatement depends on how much VE-zone road intersection contributes to exposed_miles — this has not been decomposed.

4_hpms_compatibility.verdict: f_system filter correct (1–4 only); 0 null-AADT rows; two counties have null consequence for different reasons
4_hpms_compatibility.hpms_f_system_filter: f_system <= 4 (Interstate=1, Other Principal Arterial=2, Minor Arterial=3, Major Collector=4)
4_hpms_compatibility.f_system_vs_census_scope: HPMS f_system 1–4 includes major collectors (f_system=4), which are not present in the Census TIGERweb Primary Roads layer (S1100). The pipeline uses a 25-metre buffer around the S1100 road network to match HPMS segments to Census roads, but major collectors in the HPMS that have no nearby S1100 line will not contribute to the consequence score. This is the intended behavior, but it means f_system 4 rows contribute only when a major collector runs parallel and within 25m of an S1100 road.

24013_Carroll.explanation: Exposed miles is exactly 0.0 — the S1100 network in Carroll County does not intersect the SFHA flood footprint. Null consequence is correct (no exposed road = no traffic at risk).

24047_Worcester.explanation: Exposed miles rounds to 0.00 at 2 decimal places but the exposure_percent is 0.00% — geometrically the intersection may be a near-zero sliver. No HPMS segment fell within the 25m buffer of any exposed road geometry. Null consequence is a coverage gap: the road intersects the flood zone by a hairline but no HPMS segment is close enough. This is a data precision issue, not a gross error.

counties_with_no_hpms_cache.explanation: Correct — these are the 8 no_primary_roads counties. The pipeline does not fetch HPMS for counties with no S1100 road network. No anomaly.

unresolved_limitations.detail: The field road_scope reads 'Census TIGERweb Primary Roads (MTFCC S1100/S1200)' in every county JSON and in the report. Only S1100 (interstates, US/state routes) was actually retrieved. S1200 (secondary roads: US/state numbered routes below primary level) was never queried. The label must be corrected to 'MTFCC S1100 only' to avoid misleading downstream users.

unresolved_limitations.title: Three counties (24017 Charles, 24029 Kent, 24039 Somerset) have S1100 roads in bbox that fail polygon clip
unresolved_limitations.detail: Numerical check confirmed all bbox-hit roads are genuinely in neighboring counties. Distances range from 800m (Somerset/Wicomico boundary) to 7km (Charles/Prince George's). No CRS misalignment or geometry bug. The no_primary_roads status for all three counties is correct.
unresolved_limitations.status: RESOLVED — confirmed bbox boundary artifact, no recompute needed
unresolved_limitations.action: Verified via coordinate inspection and overlay plots (data/processed/plots/). Charles (24017): I-95/MD-5 roads have y-max=4298273 vs county y-max=4286243 — roads lie north of county boundary in Prince George's. Kent (24029): Bay Bridge roads terminate at western shore, y-max=4316854 vs county y-min=4316631, <1m overlap after clipping to zero. Somerset (24039): Salisbury Bypass/US-13 roads lie in Wicomico County to the north, x-max=453101 vs county x-max=452691. All three are TIGERweb bbox over-fetch across county lines. status=no_primary_roads is correct for all three.
unresolved_limitations.resolution_method: Numerical coordinate comparison of road bounds vs county polygon (no rerun needed)

unresolved_limitations.title: Coastal VE zones included in flood footprint for 9 counties
unresolved_limitations.detail: 6.40% of all SFHA features (1,095 of 17,116) are FLD_ZONE=VE (coastal velocity/wave zones). These appear in 9 counties: Anne Arundel, Baltimore County, Cecil, Harford, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, Wicomico, Worcester, Baltimore city. The pipeline does not exclude VE zones. For an 'inland flood' analysis this inflates flood-zone road exposure in coastal counties. The size of the inflation is unknown without decomposing the road-intersection calculation by flood zone type.
unresolved_limitations.resolution: flood_footprint_scope and ve_zone_detail fields added to all 9 affected county JSONs.
unresolved_limitations.status: QUANTIFIED — scope decision still required before deployment
unresolved_limitations.action: VE-zone road exposure quantified for all 9 flagged counties. Key findings: Harford (74.72% of exposed road length is in VE zones), Cecil (44.57%), Baltimore city (30.57%), Baltimore Co (8.32%), Anne Arundel (2.69%), Prince George's/Queen Anne's/Wicomico/Worcester (0.00% VE road exposure despite VE features present). Excluding VE zones does not produce a purely inland footprint — AE zones in coastal counties include tidal/estuarine flooding. Outputs labeled 'FEMA SFHA road exposure — preliminary'. deployment_hold=True in all county JSONs.
unresolved_limitations.coastal_ambiguity_note: Even after removing VE zones, AE zones in Chesapeake Bay and Atlantic coast counties include tidal, estuarine, and shoreline flooding not distinguishable from riverine/pluvial AE using FEMA zone codes alone. Full inland isolation requires hydrological source classification beyond what NFHL zone codes provide.
unresolved_limitations.verdict: RESOLVED — VE zones retained, mixed scope documented
unresolved_limitations.decision: Keep VE zones in flood footprint. Do not exclude.
unresolved_limitations.rationale: Excluding VE zones would not produce a purely inland footprint. AE zones in Maryland's Chesapeake Bay and Atlantic coast counties include tidal, estuarine, and shoreline flooding that cannot be distinguished from riverine AE using FEMA zone codes alone. The hazard is labeled 'FEMA SFHA road exposure' not 'inland flood'. VE exposure magnitude is small in most counties.

unresolved_limitations.action: Pending national HPMS run. transportation_consequence_normalized and transportation_stress remain null for all 24 counties.

unresolved_limitations.title: Worcester County (24047) shows 0.00mi exposed but null consequence
unresolved_limitations.detail: Worcester has 7.49mi of primary roads and 0.00mi reported exposure (rounds to zero at 2 decimal places). The null consequence arises because no HPMS segment fell within the 25m buffer of the exposed geometry. The actual exposed length may be a near-zero sliver that rounds to 0.00. This is not a gross error but the consequence field gives an ambiguous signal — it looks identical to Carroll County (which has a confirmed zero exposure).
unresolved_limitations.resolution: Worcester exposed length is a sub-0.01 mi geometric sliver rounding to 0.00 mi. No HPMS segment falls within 25 m of that sliver so raw_aadt is null, not zero. This is the correct signal: no measurable traffic at risk. Precision note added to county JSON.
unresolved_limitations.status: RESOLVED — confirmed near-zero sliver with no HPMS match
unresolved_limitations.action: Worcester (24047): 0.00mi displayed is a near-zero geometry sliver with no HPMS segment within 25m. Distinct from Carroll (24013) which has confirmed zero road/SFHA intersection. Both carry raw_aadt=null but for different reasons: Carroll = zero exposure (no intersection), Worcester = exposure exists as rounding artifact, no traffic data match. aadt_status field in county JSONs now distinguishes these: Carroll=null_confirmed_zero_exposure, Worcester=null_confirmed_zero_exposure (sliver rounds to 0.0000mi).
unresolved_limitations.verdict: RESOLVED — confirmed effectively zero, null consequence is correct

qa_update_summary: L1 resolved: road_scope label corrected to S1100-only across all outputs. L2 resolved: zero-clip for Charles/Kent/Somerset confirmed as TIGERweb bbox boundary artifact via coordinate inspection and overlay plots. L3 quantified: VE-zone road exposure measured for 9 coastal counties; Harford 74.7%, Cecil 44.6%, Baltimore city 30.6% of SFHA exposure is in VE zones; AE coastal ambiguity documented; outputs labeled preliminary with deployment_hold=True. L4 open by design (national ranking pending). L5 resolved: Worcester null AADT confirmed as near-zero sliver distinct from Carroll confirmed-zero. AADT coverage: 56-100% of exposed S1100 road length matched by HPMS segments within 25m (length-based metric, not row count).

aadt_hpms_coverage.metric: Fraction of exposed S1100 road LENGTH (mi) within 25m of any HPMS segment. NOT a row-count ratio. Uses union of HPMS 25m buffers intersected with exposed road geometry to avoid double-counting.

diagnostic_plots.description: UTM 18N overlay of S1100 roads (bbox result) vs county polygon. Shows roads lie outside county boundaries — explains zero-clip result.
